source: MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture, banana cultivation techniques manual, 2019, section IV.4 (fertilizing)
text:
Banana grows fast and produces a large volume of leaf, root, and fruit tissue, so it has substantial nutrient demands; even though the plant tolerates a wide range of soils, poor nutrition will show up directly as reduced yield and poorer fruit quality. The manual gives the following fertilizing schedule, based on compound NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer unless otherwise noted, applied per clump:

- At 1 month after planting: apply about 100g of 15-15-15 per clump.
- At 3 months: apply about 200g of 15-15-15 per clump.
- At 4 months: apply a potassium fertilizer (muriate of potash, KCl), about 100g per clump, to help reduce losses and improve fruit sweetness later.
- At 6 months: apply about 150g of 15-15-15 per clump.
- At 7 months (around flowering): apply about 50-100g of 15-15-15 per clump.

Across a full year, the source also describes a complementary program of urea mixed with DAP fertilizer, about 80g per clump, applied four times per year, plus potassium fertilizer (KCl) at about 90g per clump, applied twice per year.

Practical application notes: apply fertilizer within about a 50cm radius of the base rather than right against the trunk; fertilizer can be combined with compost or manure worked in around the clump; and fertilizer should be lightly buried into the soil (rather than left on the surface) to reduce nutrient loss to evaporation/runoff and improve uptake.
